purpose: Provide the seven V2 direct-secondary load and thermal readings for questions.
title: V2 secondary-load measurements
takeaway: The loaded sequence shows falling secondary voltage and rising secondary-region temperature; it did not reach thermal equilibrium. Planning only, not visible.

visible_content.caption: V2 · direct secondary load · 240 V AC, 50 Hz
visible_content.condition: Successive load points; no thermal equilibrium

visual.layout: Dominant editable seven-row, six-column table in measurement order; native PowerPoint table with editable text. Place the condition caption above and the thermal-equilibrium line below. No body points.
visual.rounding: Secondary voltage, current and power to two decimals; thermal maxima to one decimal. Number points 1–7 in acquisition order; the original capture IDs are retained in exact_data.

speaker_notes: The electronic load was connected directly to the V2 secondary, before the USB-C PD stage. The table shows secondary power calculated from measured voltage and current. As current increased from 1.86 to 10.01 amperes, voltage fell from 26.14 to 13.69 volts and power rose from 48.68 to 137.08 watts. R3 is the input-bridge surface region and R1 is the secondary surface region. The highest R3 reading, 83.9 degrees Celsius, occurred at the intermediate point of 70.75 watts; later readings were lower, so the bridge temperatures are not monotonic with load. The R1 maximum increased from 50.3 to 98.3 degrees. These are successive load points without thermal equilibrium: the temperature changes reflect the load changes and continued heating during the sequence, rather than a settled temperature curve.
